issuer: Colorado Department of Revenue, Taxation Division
title: Colorado DOR General Information Letter GIL-26-004: Digital Photography Provided via Online Gallery
summary: Special Rule 34.5 addresses photography services and provides that they are not taxable when such service “is specifically bargained for without regard to the tangible personal property involved, and if the value of the service is greater than the [value of the] property transferred. . . .” Accordingly, when the photographs are an expressly bargained‑for component of a photography services transaction, the conditions of Special Rule 34.5 are not met. The grant of a license to use or possess tangible personal property, including a digital photograph, constitutes the transfer of a partial interest in that tangible personal property. Consequently, if the transfer is made in exchange for any consideration, it constitutes a sale under Rule 39-26-102.

Re: Digital Photography Provided via Online Gallery
Dear XXXXXXXXX:
You submitted a request for a general information letter regarding the application of sales tax to
digital photography provided via an online gallery. The Colorado Department of Revenue
(“Department”) issues general information letters and private letter rulings. A general information
letter provides a general overview of the relevant tax issues but is not binding on the
Department. A private letter ruling provides a specific determination for a specific set of facts, is
binding on the Department, and requires payment of a fee. For more information about general
information letters and private letter rulings, please see 1 C C R 201-1, Rule 24-35-103.5.
Issues
1. Whether retail sales where a client pays for a photoshoot and a license to use photos
and subsequently obtains access to those photos through an online gallery are subject
to sales tax.
2. Whether retail sales where a third party purchases a stand-alone, extended use license
for access to the same online gallery referenced in the issue above are subject to sales
tax.
Discussion
Colorado generally levies sales tax on the retail sale of tangible personal property and those
services expressly enumerated in statute.1 In the case of services rendered in the creation of
custom-made goods, Colorado imposes tax on “the full purchase price of articles sold after
manufacture or after being made to order” including the cost of services provided used to create
or produce the item.2 Services that are inseparable from the creation of the item offered for sale
are treated as part of the taxable sale.3 Tangible personal property subject to sales tax includes
1 Section 39-26-104(1)(a), C.R.S. See A.D. Store Co., Inc. v. Executive Dir. of Dept. of Rev., 19 P.3d 680, 683 (Colo. 2001).
2 Section 39-26-102(12), C.R.S.; 1 C C R 201-4, Rule 39-26-102(12).
3 A.D. Store, 19 P.3d at 683–84.

digital goods, which are “any item of tangible personal property that is delivered or stored by
digital means.”4 Methods of delivery for digital goods “include but are not limited to compact
disc, electronic download, and internet streaming.”5
Special Rule 34.5 addresses photography services and provides that they are not taxable when
such service “is specifically bargained for without regard to the tangible personal property
involved, and if the value of the service is greater than the [value of the] property
transferred. . . .”6 Accordingly, when the photographs are an expressly bargained‑for component
of a photography services transaction, the conditions of Special Rule 34.5 are not met.7
As discussed above, the retail sale of digital goods, like photographs stored in an online gallery,
is a sale of tangible personal property.8 A sale is any transaction whereby a person, in exchange
for any consideration, transfers or agrees to transfer all or part of an interest in tangible personal
property to another person.9 The grant of a license to use or possess tangible personal property
constitutes the transfer of a partial interest in such property.
Miscellaneous
This letter represents the good-faith opinion of Department personnel who are knowledgeable
on state taxes issues. However, the Department does not make a specific determination on any
of the issues raised, and the Department is not bound by this general information letter.
The Department administers state and state-administered local sales and use taxes. This letter
does not address sales and use taxes administered by self-collected home-rule cities. You may
wish to consult with those local governments that administer their own sales or use taxes about
the applicability of those taxes. Visit our website at Tax.Colorado.gov for more information about
state and local sales taxes.
Thank you for your request.
Sincerely,
Office of Tax Policy
